## 1. Reusable Reverse Engineering & Browser WASM Facts (Verified in Production)

- **Static recompilation vs emulation**: Instead of emulating an x86 CPU at runtime, `tools/recomp/lift.py` (3,334 LOC Python) lifts **13,766 32-bit x86 functions** from a 3.18 MB Windows PE binary (`Speed.exe`, MD5 `b6b9232c55376b3c38c56aac1f8a121d`, base `0x400000`) to C ahead of time, compiled via Emscripten/LLVM to WebAssembly (`42.31 MB` raw, `7.04 MB` Brotli `-q 11`).
- **Compiler passes for lifted x86**: Inter-procedural dead EFLAGS liveness pruning (`FlagABI`, `8444027`: `par(` -82.1%, `af=` -80.7%, `cf` -69.4%), `CHK_IMG` static-image bypass + straight-line `CHK_SP` stack-pointer coalescing (`69f51fb`, `fc8ef2e`: `619,768 -> 385,228` checks, `-37.8%`), and `RN_FAST_X87` verified against `RN_STRICT_X87` via single-function differential testing (`tools/recomp/difftest.py`, `5,404/5,407` pass).
- **DirectX 9 to WebGPU / WebGL 2 (`host/` `15,035` LOC C + `web/gpu.js`)**: Native DXT1/3/5 -> BC1/2/3 GPU texture passthrough (`RN_S3TC`, `00e474c`, `4x-8x` VRAM savings), compact `256 B` dynamic UBO slicing (`deb8f28`, uniform upload `~9.6 -> 1.32 MB/frame`, `-86.2%`), cached post-FX `bindGroup`s, and `unorm8x4-bgra` software fallback.
- **V8 WebAssembly code cache preservation (`653dc84`)**: Passing raw `fetch()` directly to `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(r, imports)` without `TransformStream` / `new Response()` wrappers preserves V8 disk code caching and cut JS memory at run from `58.08` to `13.22 MiB` (`-77.2%`).
- **Mobile WebAssembly memory & boot (`511830f`, `653dc84`)**: Freeing CPU-side shadow vertex/index buffers (`SmoothEnt`) after GPU upload fixed a 50-minute OOM; shrinking `speed_lite.wasm` heap to `448 MB` (`256 MB` guest RAM) enabled 4 GB phones; gating a `19.02 MiB` 3D preview curtain off mobile/low-tier cut mobile boot from `107.08 s` to `76.62 s` (`-28.4%`) and JS heap by `-79.3%`.
- **Zero-upload Cloudflare R2 / S3 immutable header migration (`tools/r2_set_immutable.py`)**: S3 `CopyObject` onto the same key with `x-amz-metadata-directive: REPLACE` updated `419/419` objects (`1.32 GB`) to `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` in seconds with 0 bytes re-uploaded.
- **Evidence-first AI reverse engineering corpus**: 49 verified subsystem monographs (2,858 unique hex addresses), 59 symbol census tables (`18,293` rows, `7,886` `V`-tagged, https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/symbols.md), and 15 modular patch sets (`753` unique addresses, https://nfsu.cc/reverse-engineering/patches.md).

## 2. Engineering Devlog (Real Commits & Measured A/B Benchmarks)

### Preserving V8 WebAssembly Code Cache, Cutting 30s Off Mobile Boot, and In-Place R2 Immutable Headers (2026-11-25)
URL: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/v8-wasm-code-cache-mobile-boot-and-r2-immutable.html | Markdown: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/v8-wasm-code-cache-mobile-boot-and-r2-immutable.md | Commits: 653dc84

Four production-measured browser engineering patterns that apply to any large WebAssembly app or Cloudflare R2 deployment, explained both in plain English (ELI5) and with real A/B Chrome benchmarks.

## ELI5: What changed and why it matters

If you build or ship heavy web apps (WebAssembly games, CAD tools, emulators, or AI runtimes), three invisible traps quietly slow down your users:

1. **Breaking the browser's shortcut memory (V8 WASM cache)**: Browsers like Chrome compile WebAssembly once and save the compiled machine code on disk so the next visit starts almost instantly. If your JavaScript intercepts the download stream to draw a progress bar (`new Response(new TransformStream(...))`), Chrome throws away the URL identity and **refuses to cache the compiled code**. Passing the raw `fetch()` response straight to `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming()` restores the cache and cuts RAM spikes by 77%.
2. **Loading a 20 MB 3D menu on a phone that only wants to start**: Showing a 3D preview scene while the real app loads looks great on a desktop GPU, but on a phone it steals bandwidth, CPU, and 18 MB of JS heap before the first real frame renders. Skipping the 3D curtain on touch/low-tier devices shaved **30.5 seconds** off mobile boot time.
3. **Updating cloud cache headers without re-uploading gigabytes**: If you forgot `Cache-Control: immutable` on 1.32 GB of static assets in Cloudflare R2 or AWS S3, you do **not** have to re-upload them. A single S3 `CopyObject` request with `MetadataDirective=REPLACE` updates the header server-side in seconds with zero upload bandwidth.

---

## Technical Deep Dive: Measured Root Causes & Fixes (`653dc84`)

### 1. Restoring V8 WebAssembly Code Caching (`web/boot.js`)

Chromium's V8 engine only caches compiled WebAssembly (`WebAssembly.Module`) to HTTP cache / disk when `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(responsePromise, imports)` receives a genuine network `Response` backed by a cacheable URL. Wrapping `response.body` in a `TransformStream` or `ReadableStream` to count bytes creates a synthetic `Response` with `response.url === ""`, which silently disables V8 code caching and buffers extra copies in JS memory.

**Fix:** Replaced the `TransformStream` progress wrapper in `web/boot.js` with a direct `fetchWithRetry(url)` passed straight into `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(r, imports)`:

```js
// Reusable pattern: preserve V8 WASM code cache on repeat visits
const res = await fetchWithRetry(wasmUrl);
const { instance } = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(res, imports);
```

**Measured A/B (desktop headless Chrome, `/?mute=1&go=1`):**

| Metric | Before (`TransformStream`) | After (Direct `instantiateStreaming`) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| JS memory at `run` (`atRunMem`) | 58.08 MiB | 13.22 MiB | **-77.2%** |
| Warm boot to `d3d9 first Present` | 715.59 ms | 674.46 ms | **-5.7%** |

### 2. Gating the 20 MB 3D Preview Curtain Off Mobile & Low-Tier (`web/index.html`)

On desktop, `launcher_b` mounts a PlayCanvas 3D street scene (`~19 MiB` of GLB/textures + WebGL context) as a visual curtain during `fast=1` boots. On coarse-pointer or low-tier devices (`RN_COARSE || RN_LOW_TIER`), that curtain competed directly with the 448 MB WASM module and asset streaming.

**Fix:** Gated the `<iframe>` mount behind `RN_Q.get('fast') === '1' && !RN_COARSE && !RN_LOW_TIER`. Desktop keeps the full 3D curtain untouched (`rnAbMs: 498 ms`, 0 JS errors).

**Measured A/B (mobile Chrome headless `844x390 dpr 2`, 4x CPU throttle, 5 Mbps / 100 ms RTT, `/?mute=1&fast=1&go=1`):**

| Metric | Before (3D Curtain Active) | After (Gated on Mobile) | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `launcher_b` transfer | 19.02 MiB | 0 B | **-100%** |
| Curtain block time (`RN_AB_MS`) | 1500 ms | 0 ms | **-100%** |
| `d3d9 first Present` | 107.08 s | 76.62 s | **-30.46 s (-28.4%)** |
| `atRunMem` | 70.32 MiB | 15.59 MiB | **-77.8%** |
| CDP `JSHeapUsedSize` | 22.29 MiB | 4.62 MiB | **-79.3%** |

### 3. Immutable Caching on Versioned Assets & Zero-Upload R2 Metadata Migration (`tools/upload_r2.sh`, `tools/r2_set_immutable.py`)

Previously, `*.js` and `/out/speed*.wasm` were uploaded with `no-cache`, forcing conditional `304` revalidation round-trips on every visit even though every URL already carries a content hash (`?v=RN_V`). Meanwhile, 419 static `game/*` files (1.32 GB) sat in `r2:nfsu` without `immutable`.

- **`tools/upload_r2.sh`**: Kept `no-cache` strictly on HTML/JSON/manifest entry points, and switched hashed `/*.js`, `/out/speed*.js`, and Brotli `-q 11` `/out/speed*.wasm` to `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- **`tools/r2_set_immutable.py`**: Wrote a zero-dependency Python stdlib AWS SigV4 script that lists `r2:nfsu/game/` and issues S3 `CopyObject` onto the same key with `x-amz-metadata-directive: REPLACE` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- **Production result**: `nfsu/game/: total=419 updated=419 skipped=0` in seconds with **0 bytes re-uploaded**.

### 4. Non-Isolated Desktop CTA & Anonymous Funnel Beacon (`web/app.js`, `tools/crash/worker.js`)

`SharedArrayBuffer` requires `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. When users open a WebAssembly app inside an in-app browser, iframe, or proxy that strips COOP/COEP, auto-reloading causes an infinite loop.

- **`web/app.js`**: When `crossOriginIsolated === false` on desktop, renders a clean direct-open + copy-link CTA instead of looping.
- **`tools/crash/worker.js` + `tools/crash/read_funnel.sh`**: Extended the Cloudflare Worker on `/crash` to accept a compact, allowlisted `rn-funnel-1` JSON event (<=1024 B, zero PII) written to a disjoint `funnel/YYYY-MM-DD/` R2 prefix so crash logs stay clean while conversion (`run` vs `stop`) and `load_ms` p50/p90 are measurable by OS and tier.

### Hunting a 50-Minute Browser OOM and Shrinking Mobile WASM to 448 MB (2026-11-24)
URL: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/production-crash-hardening-and-448mb-phone-wasm.html | Markdown: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/production-crash-hardening-and-448mb-phone-wasm.md | Commits: 511830f, 921e827

Shipping a statically recompiled 2003 PC game to thousands of real browsers surfaces failure modes that desktop tests never hit. Here is what production telemetry caught and how two surgical patches fixed both long-session OOMs and low-RAM phone crashes.

## What real browsers broke in production

Once `nfsu.cc` went live, every unhandled browser crash reported a small JSON payload to our Cloudflare R2 crash bucket (`r2:nfsu-crash`). Auditing real user sessions revealed two distinct classes of failure:

1. **Memory exhaustion on phones and long desktop sessions**: `speed_lite.wasm` previously requested a 640 MB initial heap, which caused iOS Safari and 4 GB Android devices to fail WebAssembly instantiation (`could not allocate memory`), while long 50-minute desktop sessions slowly accumulated CPU-side geometry memory.
2. **Browser API edge cases**: GPUs without `unorm8x4-bgra` vertex format support, browsers missing `Atomics.waitAsync`, `tsBuf.unmap()` races on timestamp queries, transient network drops during chunk/WASM fetches, and `IndexedDB` hangs on save boot.

## Cutting the 50-minute OOM and dropping `speed_lite.wasm` to 448 MB (`511830f`)

Three concrete changes eliminated the memory pressure without touching original 2003 gameplay or audio:

- **Freeing CPU-side `SmoothEnt` buffers after GPU upload (`host/d3d9.c`)**: On web builds, once smoothed vertex and index buffers are uploaded to WebGPU/WebGL 2, keeping the host-side CPU shadow copy around caused linear memory growth across races. Freeing them immediately after upload stopped the 50-minute OOM.
- **Lowering `speed_lite.wasm` heap from 640 MB to 448 MB (`tools/recomp/build.py`, `host/host.h`)**: `GUEST_MEM` on the lite build was tightened to 256 MB and total WASM memory to 448 MB, letting budget Android phones and iPhones allocate the module cleanly.
- **Tightening transient host allocations (`host/files.c`, `host/main.c`)**: Desktop block cache cap (`blk_cap`) was reduced from 256 MB to 128 MB, and the temporary PE image buffer (`pe`) is now freed immediately after Win32 import resolution completes.

## Hardening the WebGPU, audio, and network host (`921e827`)

- **WebGPU `unorm8x4-bgra` software fallback (`web/gpu.js`)**: Devices that reject `unorm8x4-bgra` vertex attributes now fall back cleanly instead of throwing during pipeline creation.
- **Guarded timestamp query unmap (`web/gpu.js`)**: Prevented invalid-state throws when `tsBuf.unmap()` raced with device teardown.
- **`Atomics.waitAsync` fallback (`web/boot.js`)**: Older browser engines without `Atomics.waitAsync` no longer abort worker startup.
- **Network retries and clean shutdown (`web/boot.js`, `host/files.c`)**: Fetch and WASM download paths retry transient failures, `IndexedDB` open calls have bounded timeouts (`web/saves.js`), audio degrades gracefully instead of crashing when autoplay/context fails (`web/audio.js`), and `ExitProcess(0)` closes cleanly.

## Takeaway for browser static recompilation

Emulators usually cap memory tightly up front; static recompilations inherit the original PC executable's allocation assumptions plus a host GPU translation layer. Pairing a lightweight crash beacon with strict CPU-shadow freeing after GPU upload is what makes a 2003 Windows binary survive real mobile browsers.

### Static Recompiler Optimizations: Dead x86 Flag Pruning, CHK_SP Coalescing, and Fast x87 (2026-11-23)
URL: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/recompiler-dead-flags-chk-sp-fast-x87.html | Markdown: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/recompiler-dead-flags-chk-sp-fast-x87.md | Commits: 8444027, 69f51fb, fc8ef2e

Naive x86-to-C static recompilation spends most of its CPU budget updating EFLAGS nobody reads and bounds-checking ESP on every push and pop. Here is how tools/recomp/lift.py eliminates both while staying verified by difftest.py.

## The cost of faithful x86 lifting

`pc/Speed.exe` (3.18 MB, 2003 PC) contains **13,764 functions** lifted ahead of time into C by `tools/recomp/lift.py` and compiled to `web/out/speed.wasm` (42.31 MB uncompressed, ~11.1 MB brotli). In early builds, every arithmetic instruction computed `CF`, `ZF`, `SF`, `OF`, and `PF`, and every stack/memory access emitted a runtime bounds check.

## 1. Liveness-based dead guest flag pruning (`8444027`)

In x86 code, the vast majority of flag writes are overwritten by the next `add`, `sub`, `xor`, or `inc` before any conditional branch (`jcc`), `cmov`, `setcc`, or `adc`/`sbb` ever reads them.

- `tools/recomp/lift.py` and `tools/recomp/abk.py` now compute intra- and inter-procedural **flag liveness** (`FlagABI` argument and live-flag masks across direct `call_to(target)` edges).
- Instructions whose flag outputs are dead emit plain C integer math (`eax = eax + ecx;`) instead of flag-computing helper calls.
- Special control-flow edges (`popfd`, indirect calls, traps, and return boundaries) conservatively preserve live flag masks so semantics never drift.

## 2. `CHK_IMG` and straight-line `CHK_SP` coalescing (`69f51fb`, `fc8ef2e`)

Guest memory safety in `host/rt.h` prevents a bug in lifted x86 from corrupting the Emscripten host heap, but checking every individual stack slot inside a function prologue/epilogue is wasteful:

- **`CHK_IMG`**: Constant addresses known to lie inside the static PE image (`0x400000+`) bypass dynamic range checks.
- **`CHK_SP` coalescing**: Within any straight-line basic block (broken at loop targets and overlap-stream entries), `lift.py` tracks `esp` deltas (`sp_acc` / `sp_move`) and emits **one coalesced stack bounds check** covering the block's min/max stack excursion instead of one check per `push`/`pop`.
- **Cold trap path (`host/rt.h`)**: Bounds-check failure paths are marked cold so Clang/LLVM keeps the hot WebAssembly loop tight.

## 3. `RN_FAST_X87` verified against `RN_STRICT_X87` (`69f51fb`)

x87 floating-point stack emulation is a classic hotspot in 2003 PC racing physics (`physics.md`, `accel.md`). `host/rt.h` now splits x87 execution into:

- **`RN_FAST_X87`** for shipped game builds (fast native IEEE-754 doubles in WASM registers).
- **`RN_STRICT_X87`** for `tools/recomp/difftest.py` trace builds, allowing single-function differential verification (`RN_ONLY=<addr> tools/recomp/difftest.py`) against reference traces whenever a compiler pass changes.

### DirectX 9 to WebGPU & WebGL 2: Native BC1/2/3 Textures and a Zero-Waste Draw Pipeline (2026-11-23)
URL: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/zero-waste-webgpu-draw-pipeline-and-bc-textures.html | Markdown: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/zero-waste-webgpu-draw-pipeline-and-bc-textures.md | Commits: deb8f28, 00e474c

Translating a 2003 DirectX 9 renderer to WebGPU (with automatic WebGL 2 fallback) is easy to make correct and hard to make fast. Two rendering passes removed the biggest CPU and VRAM bottlenecks.

## Keeping DXT1/3/5 textures compressed as BC1/2/3 (`00e474c`)

Need for Speed Underground ships its car liveries, road surfaces, and Olympic City environment textures as DirectX DXT1, DXT3, and DXT5 blocks. Earlier browser builds decoded those blocks to uncompressed RGBA8 on the CPU before uploading them, multiplying VRAM usage by 4x to 8x and stalling frame times during streaming.

Commit `00e474c` introduced **`RN_S3TC`** end-to-end:

- **`host/d3d9.c`**: Detects hardware block-compression support and passes raw DXT1/3/5 mip bytes straight through the host GPU command stream without CPU decompression.
- **`web/gpu.js` (WebGPU)**: Requests `texture-compression-bc` when available and uploads directly to `bc1-rgba-unorm`, `bc2-rgba-unorm`, and `bc3-rgba-unorm` textures.
- **`web/webgpu_gl.js` (WebGL 2 fallback)**: Uses `WEBGL_compressed_texture_s3tc` (`compressedTexImage2D`) so browsers without WebGPU still get the same 4x-8x VRAM savings and zero-decode uploads.
- **Upload counters**: Boot logs track compressed vs uncompressed texture uploads so regressions are immediately visible.

## Zero-waste draw pipeline, compact dynamic UBO, and post `bindGroup` cache (`deb8f28`)

DirectX 9 games issue hundreds of small stateful draw calls per frame (changing a single transform matrix, light constant, or texture stage). In WebGPU, naively allocating a fresh uniform buffer or `GPUBindGroup` per draw call creates severe JS garbage-collection pressure.

Commit `deb8f28` overhauled `host/d3d9.c`, `host/gpu.c`, `host/sm1.c`, and `web/gpu.js`:

- **Compact dynamic UBO layout**: Packed shader uniforms tightly so each draw call slices a single pre-allocated dynamic uniform buffer via `setBindGroup(..., [dynamicOffset])`.
- **Zero-waste draw state**: Avoided redundant state writes and shader-constant re-uploads when consecutive draws share transforms or materials.
- **Post-process `bindGroup` cache**: Cached post-processing bind groups (bloom, motion blur, tone pass) instead of rebuilding them every frame.

### One URL for Desktops and Phones: Frame-Time Quality Control and Dual WASM Builds (2026-11-22)
URL: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/adaptive-frame-time-quality-and-dual-wasm-builds.html | Markdown: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/adaptive-frame-time-quality-and-dual-wasm-builds.md | Commits: 40e6aff, b9c9753, e19daa6, c8e94a4, 9545ee5

Users open nfsu.cc on everything from M4 Macs and RTX desktops to budget Android phones. Instead of forcing manual tuning, the page measures its own frame times and adapts live.

## Always-on 256-frame present ring (`40e6aff`)

You cannot tune performance from guesswork. `host/d3d9.c` now maintains a lightweight ring buffer of the last **256 `Present()` intervals**, exposed to `web/stats.js`. Every windowed p50/p95 frame-time summary feeds both live diagnostics (`rnReport`) and crash telemetry lines so slow devices are immediately identifiable.

## Closed-loop frame-time quality controller (`b9c9753`, `c8e94a4`)

`web/quality.js` observes real measured frame times and steps down (or up) in a strict visual-preservation order:

`resolution -> motion blur -> post effects -> fps target -> quality tier`

- Measured tiers persist in `localStorage` (`rn_quality`) so repeat visits start smoothly.
- If a device stays above `p50 > 100 ms` across two windows even on `ultralite`, the UI surfaces a clean below-the-floor notice (`c8e94a4`) instead of silently freezing.
- On `ultralite`, **the full 2003 soundtrack is preserved** (`9545ee5`): cutting the music breaks the identity of Need for Speed Underground, so audio stays intact while pixels and post-FX scale.

## Shipping `speed_lite.wasm` alongside `speed.wasm` (`e19daa6`)

`tools/build_public.py` and `tools/upload_r2.sh` publish both `out/speed.wasm` (desktop) and `out/speed_lite.wasm` (phones/tablets) pre-compressed with **Brotli `-q 11 -w 24`** directly on Cloudflare R2, served with `Content-Encoding: br` and `Content-Type: application/wasm`. The browser downloads ~11 MB once and streams only the 2003 game chunks needed for the next screen.

### Opening the Complete Reverse Engineering Atlas of Speed.exe (44 Subsystems) (2026-11-24)
URL: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/reverse-engineering-44-subsystems-of-speed-exe.html | Markdown: https://nfsu.cc/devlog/reverse-engineering-44-subsystems-of-speed-exe.md | Commits: 9776828

Recompiling a 2003 binary without source code requires understanding how the game actually works inside. Today we are publishing all 44 reverse-engineering system notes from docs/re/ directly on nfsu.cc/re/.

## Why publish the full binary atlas

Most retro web ports are black boxes. `RE-NFSU` was built on an evidence-first rule: every claim about `Speed.exe` (md5 `b6b9232c55376b3c38c56aac1f8a121d`, base `0x400000`, 3.18 MB) must cite the exact address or bytes read in the binary, tagged **V** (verified in code/bytes), **I** (inferred), or **U** (open).

Across the repository, that effort produced:

- **44 subsystem monographs** in [`docs/re/`](https://nfsu.cc/re/index.html): car physics, acceleration curves, tuning math, chase/speed/jump/crash cameras, rival rubber-banding and AI stuck detection, traffic pools and reactions, track splines and Road IDs, DirectX 8/9 render pipeline, motion blur, sound banks, garage/career gameflow, and asset pack formats.
- **57 symbol census tables** (`census/names_*.tsv`) naming thousands of `Speed.exe` functions across every subsystem.
- **14 surgical patch modules** (`tools/recomp/patches_*.py`), where every patch cites the exact `Speed.exe` address it modifies while leaving **Original 2003** mode untouched.

## Built for humans and AI coding/search agents

Every page in the [Reverse Engineering Atlas](https://nfsu.cc/re/index.html) and [Engineering Devlog](https://nfsu.cc/devlog/index.html) is served both as semantic HTML (`TechArticle` JSON-LD) and as a clean **`.md` sibling** (`<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`), indexed in [`/llms.txt`](https://nfsu.cc/llms.txt), [`/llms-full.txt`](https://nfsu.cc/llms-full.txt), and [`/feed.xml`](https://nfsu.cc/feed.xml).

Whether you are researching static recompilation (alongside projects like N64Recomp, XenonRecomp, and NFSU2Recomp), digging into Black Box's 2003 racing physics, or querying an AI assistant about how a 2003 x86 `.exe` runs on WebGPU, you can inspect the primary evidence directly.
